profile: Researcher in orofacial pain with a primary focus on epidemiological, clinical, and epigenetic studies of painful temporomandibular disorder (p-TMD). In September 2026, she defended her PhD dissertation, "Painful temporomandibular disorders and headache in young adulthood: early-life factors and multidimensional clinical characterization," at Aarhus University, integrating prospective cohort analyses from the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC) with clinical phenotyping to examine early-life and lifestyle-related determinants of p-TMD in young adulthood. As a Postdoctoral Researcher, she now leads the project "Life-course and epigenetic analyses of painful temporomandibular disorders," investigating epigenetic mechanisms (including genome-wide DNA methylation) underlying vulnerability to p-TMD, building on the data and biological samples collected during her PhD.
